clue.text: Do trick?

parts.note: a do is a party, and a trick is the turn someone performs at one, so the clue describes a well-worn routine wheeled out at social gatherings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb ordering someone to perform a trick; read it as the noun, a party, and the trick becomes the one performed there.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a familiar turn or trick someone performs to entertain guests at a social gathering.

clue.text: Washing line moved for plant

indicators.note: moved tells us the letter for line shifts to another spot within the washing word

parts.note: ablution is a formal word for washing oneself

explanation.surface: Someone has shifted the washing line to make room for a plant in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' shifts the L of ABLUTION from third place to sixth.
explanation.definitionFit: Abutilon is a genus of flowering shrubs in the mallow family, often called flowering maple.

clue.text: Once called Type 150 surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of type and the numeral turn up in an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A vintage model, the Type 150, was once given a surprising name.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past participle meaning named, so it fits a phrase about what something was formerly called.

clue.text: Which one of these was cycling round grass and water hazard?

indicators.note: round says the cycled letters go around the grass word
cycling sends the last letter of the word for that vessel round to the front

parts.note: each of these wartime German craft was a sub, so the clue refers to its own answer
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: A quiz question: which of these was cycling round the grass and the water hazard on a golf course?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: each of 'these' was a submarine. 'cycling' moves its last letter to the front. 'Water hazard' borrows golf's term for a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: German submarines were a deadly danger to shipping, so a hazard lurking in the water is a fair, playful description.

clue.text: 60% off comparable jumper

indicators.note: comparable has ten letters; taking six of them away, three from each end, is sixty per cent off

explanation.surface: A sale offers a similar sweater at sixty per cent off.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% off' strips COM and BLE from the ends of COMPARABLE. 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, as British English calls one, but here it is a parachutist.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper is a soldier trained to jump from aircraft, and this short form names one.

clue.text: 23D/8's dismissive response about money

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: rats! is an exclamation brushing something off with annoyance
bucks is slang for dollars, so money

explanation.surface: A big company gives a curt, dismissive reply when asked about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RATS into STAR. 23D/8 is GLOBAL BRAND, the theme answer that serves as the definition in many clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The coffee chain is one of the best-known worldwide brand names, with branches in many countries.

clue.text: Conclude a minimal amount of settlement's best

indicators.note: a minimal amount means just one letter, the first, taken from the following word

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Accept a minimal amount: that is the best settlement on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To conclude is to finish or bring something to a halt, the same as ceasing.

clue.text: Fish served up's a kipper

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: eels are fish
per means a, as in five pounds a head

explanation.surface: A fish served up turns out to be a kipper, the smoked herring of a British breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns EELS into SLEE. 'Kipper' looks like the smoked herring; it is someone who kips, British slang for sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: To kip is to sleep in British slang, so a kipper is a person who sleeps.

clue.text: See 23
Theatre performers likely to be wooden?

definitions.text: Theatre performers likely to be wooden?

parts.words: Theatre performers likely to be wooden?
parts.note: wooden suggests stiff acting, but the clue means the backstage people who help actors into costume, and also kitchen cupboards made of wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a jibe at stiff acting. It also fits the wooden sideboards of the same name; the theatre ones are backstage staff, not performers.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre these are staff who help actors change costume; the same word names wooden sideboards with shelves for crockery.

clue.text: Can seem a thousand short

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the word for seem goes without the thousand

parts.note: to look is to seem, as in look tired
K stands for a thousand, as in a 50K salary

explanation.surface: A tin can seems a thousand short of the count.
explanation.definitionFit: Can and loo are both informal words for a lavatory.

clue.text: Exposed shady businessman after tip-off

indicators.note: after the tip is taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a tout resells tickets at inflated prices, a shady trade

explanation.surface: A shady dealer is exposed after someone tips off the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip-off' looks like an informer's warning; it means the tip, the first letter, comes off.
explanation.definitionFit: When a secret is exposed it is revealed or made public, which is what being out means.

clue.text: Subject that's habitually exasperating from the start to this setter

indicators.note: from the start says to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so me

explanation.surface: The setter complains of a subject that is always exasperating to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, this puzzle has one: GLOBAL BRAND runs through many clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic or subject of a talk, essay or puzzle is its unifying idea.

clue.text: Defy expectations with 23D/8 not on drugs

indicators.note: not means the word on is removed from the retailer's name

parts.note: the online retailer is a global brand, the theme answer
E is slang for ecstasy, so drugs

explanation.surface: Someone surprises everyone by staying clean, with a major brand not involved in drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to do the unexpected, so defying expectations is another way to say it.

clue.text: 23D/8 takes time but it does perform task

parts.note: the computer company is a global brand, the theme answer

explanation.surface: A big tech company takes its time, but its product does the job in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small program designed to carry out one specific job, often inside another application.

clue.text: Declined to tuck into vegetables and old bread

indicators.note: tuck into means go inside, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: peas are vegetables
the sun set, meaning it went down or declined

explanation.surface: Someone refused to eat their vegetables and stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined to tuck into' looks like refusing food, but 'Declined' means went down, as the sun does. 'Bread' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and these were Spain's currency before the euro, so they are former money.

clue.text: Trump's chopper finally landed amongst others — some 23D/8s, perhaps?

indicators.note: amongst says the chopper and the letter go inside the other word

parts.note: todgers is British slang for penises, so 'others' means more choppers in the vulgar sense
ax is the American spelling of axe, a chopper, so it suits an American president

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of Trump's helicopter landing among others, alongside a dig at big companies avoiding tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' is a helicopter on the surface; in British slang it is also a penis, so 'others' are more of those, in the slang plural. The American spelling of the axe suits Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: Several multinational brands have been accused of avoiding tax, so some of them could be called evaders.

clue.text: Very sad song upset a certain 23D/8

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the song word reads backwards

parts.note: fado is a mournful Portuguese song style
one means a certain, as in one Mr Smith

explanation.surface: A very sad song upsets a certain big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FADO into ODAF.
explanation.definitionFit: The mobile network operator is a household name worldwide, an example of a global brand.

clue.text: Coe ordered an Indian? Maybe

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Sebastian Coe, the British athlete, orders an Indian meal, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a curry; with 'Maybe' it is an example of a sea, like the Atlantic or the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great seas, so it is an example of this.

clue.text: Hurt — hit hard in return

indicators.note: in return means the word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: to ram is to strike with force

explanation.surface: Someone was hurt and hit back hard in retaliation.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or damage something, such as a blemish on a polished surface, is to harm it.

clue.text: Police turned up and expressed doubt after second bit

indicators.note: after places the police and doubt pieces behind the second

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second, as in wait a mo

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives
um is a hesitant noise expressing doubt

explanation.surface: The police turned up and voiced doubts after a second look at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns CID into DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A small quantity of something, as in a shred of decency, is a little piece or amount.

clue.text: Sociable type wants gender reassignment — he (or she) will sort it

indicators.note: gender reassignment swaps male for female, so the M becomes F

parts.note: a good mixer is someone who socialises easily

explanation.surface: A sociable person wants a gender change, and someone will sort it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gender reassignment' swaps M (male) for F (female), and the definition's '(or she)' nods to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges things or solves problems for others, often unofficially, is a fixer.

clue.text: 23D/8 giving nothing? Be upset having to do without

parts.note: FA is sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: without means outside, so the cooking word goes around the other

parts.note: to do food is to cook it, as in do the potatoes

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: be is taken as written

explanation.surface: A big brand gives nothing away, and people are upset at having to go without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BE into EB, which COOK holds 'without' (outside) it.
explanation.definitionFit: The social network is one of the most recognised company names worldwide.

clue.text: Supported President Kennedy perhaps over ending of threat

indicators.note: over here places one piece after another in the run of letters

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US President

indicators.note: ending of picks the final letter of the next word

parts.note: Ted Kennedy was a US senator, an example of a Kennedy

explanation.surface: A Kennedy backed the President in the face of a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet someone is to assist or encourage them, typically in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Ring fighter moved fast and picked up gold

parts.note: tore means rushed, as in tore down the road

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A boxer moves fast and wins the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring fighter' suggests a boxer; the ring is a bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter on foot fights in the bullring, which is the ring meant here.

clue.text: Heard Douglas part with small animals

indicators.note: heard means we want a word that is pronounced like the character's name

parts.note: Gordon Gekko is the role Michael Douglas played in the film Wall Street

explanation.surface: We hear that Douglas played a part alongside some small animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' looks like an adjective for the animals; it gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: These small lizards are animals, making it a broad but fair category.

clue.text: Very big player making good money: 'Chuck a pound in'

indicators.note: in says the chuck-a-pound letters go into the money word

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, good money
to lob is to throw or chuck
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A big player making good money urges: chuck a pound in.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the puzzle's theme and the definition in many clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A company name recognised worldwide is a major presence in its market, a very big player.

clue.text: Move away from 23D/8 — not a nice look

indicators.note: from here means taken out of the brand name

parts.note: the search engine is a global brand, the theme answer
to go is to move away

explanation.surface: Turning away from a big brand is not a good look.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare at someone with leering, unwelcome interest is an unpleasant way to look.

clue.text: Take place of officer in charge, a contemptible fellow

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding, officer in charge
a cur is a worthless, contemptible man

explanation.surface: Someone takes the place of the officer in charge, a contemptible man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take place of' looks like replacing someone; the definition is just 'Take place'.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen or come about is to take place.

clue.text: Steer youngster away from lousy companies — initially awkward

indicators.note: awkward suggests those letters sit clumsily and must be rearranged
initially takes the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Advice to steer a young person away from bad company, which is awkward at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb meaning guide; it is the young ox.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is a young castrated bull, and its offspring stage is the young bovine.

clue.text: Groom crosses over valley

indicators.note: crosses means the groom word stretches across the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to comb hair is to groom it
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A groom crosses over a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like a man at his wedding or a stable hand; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short hollow valley on a hillside, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Crack team doesn't have name

indicators.note: doesn't have means the word for team loses that letter

parts.note: a gang is a team of workers

explanation.surface: An elite team has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective, as in crack troops; it is a noun, a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a quip or wisecrack, and a gag is a joke.

clue.text: He must contain winger that's no good in the air

definitions.text: winger that's no good in the air

indicators.note: contain says the answer is held within the letters of the words he and must

explanation.surface: A footballer must include a winger who is weak at headers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a football player; it is a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Australian bird has wings but cannot fly.

clue.text: Rule out arresting English mathematician

indicators.note: arresting means seizing hold of, so the jumbled letters enclose the other
out signals the word is disordered, put out of shape

explanation.surface: A ruling excludes the arrest of an English mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RULE as EULR, and 'arresting' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: One in bed with rude woman getting end away — sweetheart furious

indicators.note: furious suggests the remaining letters are thrown into wild disorder
getting the end away means losing the final letter of those words

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A risqué scene of someone in bed with a rude woman, with an angry sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting end away' (British slang for having sex) drops the N. 'furious' rearranges RUDEWOMA as MEADOWRU. 'One in bed' means a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plant of the buttercup family, grown as one specimen in a flowerbed.
